newsitem.title: USA: Executive Jet orders Raytheon aircraft.
newsitem.headline: Executive Jet orders Raytheon aircraft.

text.p: Raytheon Aircraft, a subsidiary of Raytheon Co, said Executive Jet Inc ordered 20 Hawker 800XP aircrafts valued at more than $210 million.
Raytheon said Executive Jet has options for 10 more Hawker 800XP jets and has purchased an additional Hawker 1000 that was initially used for certification testing and flight demonstrations.
Executive Jet will use the new aircraft for its "NetJets" fractional aircraft ownership operation. The "NetJets" program allows companies to buy shares in business jets.
Executive Jet said it will accept delivery of its first two Raytheon Aircraft Hawker 800XPs later this year, with the remaining aircraft to be delivered over the next five years.
Executive Jet currently flies 22 Hawker 1000s in its fractional ownership operation and is extending its use of the Hawker 1000s for another five years.

At a press conference to announce the deal, Raytheon Aircraft Chairman Art Wegner said Raytheon has studied the possibility of moving into the fractional aircraft ownership business, instead of just supplying the planes to companies such as Executive Jet.
"We have looked very hard at that possibility. But we're not prepared to make an announcement yet," Wegner said.
Executive Jet Chairman Richard Santulli said he would welcome new competition because it would help expand the market.
"We've always said we'd rather have 80 percent of a larger market than 99 percent of a smaller market," Santulli said.
"But we have no assurance from Raytheon, nor did we ask for that assurance, that they would not compete with us," Santulli said.
Executive Jet, based in Montvale, N.J., manages the largest fleet of Hawker business jets in the world for corporate and individual clients.
Raytheon Aircraft manufactures and supports jet aircraft as well as turboprop and piston-powered aircraft for the world's commercial, military and regional airline markets.
